sentences.text: that it is on the basis of the enmity of the local people, the First Information Report has been instituted against the appellant.
4. Mrs. Nehala Sharmin, learned Spl.P.P. appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer to interfere with the impugned order.
5. The ground of opposition is based upon the statement so recorded in the Case Diary.
She has also taken the ground that the trial is in progress and as such it would not be proper at this stage to allow the prayer for bail since there is chances of tampering with the evidence.

6. Upon this submission, learned counsel for the appellant has sought for leave of this Court not pressing this appeal, however, it is prayed that since the trial is in progress and as such, learned counsel for the State may be directed to produce the witnesses as and when summoned so that there may not be any hindrance in the conclusion of the trial.

7. Learned Spl.P.P. appearing for the State has submitted that there will not be delay in production of the witnesses so that the trial, which has already commenced, be concluded without any unnecessary delay.
8. Considering the above, this Criminal Appeal is dismissed as not pressed.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Sanjay Prasad, J.) s.m.
